India is a growing business destination for foreign companies seeking to expand their operations and access the Indian market. Foreign businesses can establish a presence in India through different legal structures, depending on their business objectives, investment requirements, and applicable regulatory conditions. Understanding the available options, incorporation process, and ongoing compliance requirements is essential before establishing a business presence in India.
Ways for Foreign Companies to Enter India
Foreign companies can establish their presence in India through the following structures:

A foreign company can establish a wholly owned subsidiary in India by incorporating a private limited company under the Companies Act, 2013. This structure may be suitable where 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is permitted in the relevant sector, subject to applicable conditions.

A foreign company can enter into a joint venture with an Indian company or investor. This structure allows the parties to share ownership, resources, expertise, and business responsibilities, subject to applicable FDI and regulatory requirements.

A liaison office can be established to represent the foreign parent company, explore business opportunities, facilitate communication, and promote its interests in India. A liaison office generally cannot undertake commercial activities or earn income in India.

A branch office is an extension of the foreign company and may undertake permitted activities such as export and import, consultancy, research, and other activities approved under applicable regulations. Its activities are subject to the conditions prescribed by the relevant authorities.

A foreign company may establish a project office in India for executing a specific project or contract. This structure can be suitable for foreign businesses involved in construction, infrastructure, engineering, and other project-based activities.
Process of Incorporating a Foreign Company in India
The incorporation process generally involves the following steps:
Determine the appropriate structure based on the nature of the proposed business, ownership requirements, investment plans, and applicable FDI and regulatory provisions.

Where required, the proposed directors must obtain a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) and Director Identification Number (DIN) for completing electronic filings with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA).
Select a suitable name and apply for name reservation through the applicable MCA process. The proposed name must comply with the prescribed naming guidelines.

Prepare the required incorporation documents, which may include the Memorandum of Association (MoA), Articles of Association (AoA), identity and address documents, declarations, and documents relating to the foreign parent company.

For an Indian subsidiary, the applicable incorporation forms, including SPICe+, are submitted electronically to the Registrar of Companies (RoC), along with the required documents and prescribed fees.
Step 6: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation
After the application is reviewed and approved, the RoC issues the Certificate of Incorporation, confirming the legal existence of the Indian company.
After incorporation, the company may need to obtain PAN and TAN, complete applicable GST registration, open a business bank account, and meet other tax and regulatory requirements.

Foreign companies establishing a presence in India must comply with applicable provisions of the , Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulations, FDI policies, the Companies Act, tax laws, and sector-specific regulations.

Depending on the structure and nature of operations, compliance obligations may include maintaining proper financial records, filing applicable returns and financial statements, meeting tax requirements, reporting foreign investments, and submitting prescribed filings to the relevant authorities.
